Detachment, directed by Tony Kaye of American History X fame, follows Adrien Brody's Henry, a drifting substitute teacher who struggles to inspire the students to take an interest in their education, as the educational system around him and his colleagues crumbles. A traditional setup in a lot of ways, but Detachment separates itself through its script and its editing, a mismatch of filmmaking styles, and a multitude of different character perspectives. The result is a relentless whirlwind of misery that, despite its best efforts, I failed to connect with. Detachment was written by Carl Lund, an interesting figure in the film industry, with only one writing credit to this day. What we do know, however, is that he used to be a public-school teacher, which quickly becomes apparent through this script — a raw and direct story that clearly comes from a place of personal rage and frustration. The movie is heavily critical of the state of the educational system, with each character serving as a vessel that represents a different struggle. Whether it be pressures from budget cuts, parents' unrealistic expectations of the school, or children with a struggling home life, it's all in here in one big — depressing — package. The result is a very nihilistic movie that offers little to no hope in its story. I'm not opposed to bleakness in film — Mike Leigh's Naked (1993), a British classic, also happens to be drenched in bleakness, with characters that embody the darkest outlooks on life, with little to no hope to be found. Detachment presents itself in a similar vein but lacks the narrative focus found in Leigh's classic. The movie clocks in at around one hour and thirty minutes but features multiple perspectives from a wide array of characters, which it struggles to juggle. There is a talented ensemble cast curated here, but most of the runtime is dedicated to Brody's character. Brody is competent in the role, but it was never clear why this character was the focal point — he's not a particularly likeable character, and even in moments where he does a good deed, he does so with a dejected and defeated energy, making him feel predictable and unengaging. Marcia Gay Harden's character felt like the more interesting focal point, with her pressures kicking off the story. Not only was her character more intriguing, but with the movie covering multiple teachers, students, and parents, her character being the headteacher would have made for a much better narrative framework to connect all these characters and bring a more natural focus. The juggling nature of Detachment also carries through into its filmmaking. Tonally, as we cut between Brody's shift in the classroom and his extracurricular miseries, the film switches from dreamlike, surreal composition — like that of a Terrence Malick film — to a more grounded, documentarian shooting style. Both styles feel at odds with each other and never come together in a satisfying way. Chaotic energy is part of the film's DNA, and the editing does a lot to feed that through: fast-paced cutting, continuity errors, intercutting between perspectives. Some may argue that this is an intentional choice given the themes, but after a while it becomes overbearing. Heat's (1995) famous bank-robbery shootout scene hits as hard as it does not just because the action is so exhilarating, but also because the editing kicks into a different gear. The moment works because the edit contrasts with the rest of the film — Detachment never allows itself that same contrast. With so many different characters and perspectives, all rendered in that same frantic style, there's nothing to alleviate the gloom. What can't be argued is that Detachment comes from a place of real conviction. Carl's script is full of despair and rage, and the themes of his writing have been successfully translated to the screen. However, I just wish the film had a little more restraint.

This film is often poorly acted, amateurishly shot in a way I don't personally like, and written rather weakly. It loses me a lot on the emotional aspects because it feels like it's trying too hard sometimes and yet simultaneously not hard enough to make me feel things. It's also sometimes a little sexist and racist if you think about it. Having said all that, I do appreciate the very honest grit this film has. It has some charm in spite of my dislike of certain aspects. It's an honesty I want more of from all art, and a vulnerability to tell something meaningful regardless of if you have the craftsmanship to see it through fully. It failed but it did so earnestly, I think that's worth something. While this story may be pretentious, I am posttentious. All things considered, I would recommend it. Detachment hooked me with its premise, but unfortunately, it didn’t quite hold up with its own narrative. While it tackled important themes like trauma, isolation, and the struggles within the education system, it ended up feeling like a string of tragic subplots being ticked off a checklist rather than one cohesive story. There was so much going on that I kept asking myself, “What’s happening? What’s this even about?” As the film kept introducing new tragedies without giving any of them enough time to fully resonate, I found myself becoming less and less invested. It became so dependent on piling on misery to make its point that, for me, it completely lost the emotional impact it was aiming for.

Naw, I'd just work at Petco or something... One helluva gritty film... Adrien Brody plays a substitute teacher working at one of the roughest schools in the district. Though he's able to handle everything well, he has own personal problems and struggles under the weight of them. It's the bleak antithesis to those hopeful films where a teacher comes in and transforms the lives of the worst behaved students... Not even one second in this classroom and they're already threatening to beat his ass. Meanwhile, he remains stoic and handles his business without missing a beat. Brody is easily the greatest part of the film. The genius of this title is that you find its meaning through his persona where he's just so focused on doing what he needs to do, not letting a single thing get to him. Though he's primarily the focus, you also see just how many teachers are dealing with it. Some of them are struggling to keep it together and some have long sense just given in to the sheer insanity of it. Even in this, surprisingly lily white, school there are some kids in particular that are so deranged that they're destined to go and become the next Charles Manson. Some even threaten to do terrible things to the teachers. Each of their subplots shows that it's an endless cycle of abuse. Hell, after calmly enduring some petty shit on his first day, you see our protagonist go off on a healthcare worker. ( And yet...who shall weep for the nurses... ) On the messaging... I would absolutely be lying if I said that it didn't feel preachy in a way that feels more over-the-top, especially when they really hammer in the point that the parents are to blame for all of this. Some of the melodramatic piano music kinda lays it on way too thick rather than just letting the scenes speak for themselves. It never truly earns the emotion that it desperately wants you to have. Oftentimes, it's borderline darkly humorous simply because of how fucking insane this community is. It's like a damn hate sink where everyone is ready to attack any teacher that walks into that building. The speed at which he is falsely accused of being inappropriate, even when he got to know this teacher more closely than any of them, before they drop it seems like it was being evil just for the hell of it. While I understand that the students aren't meant to be the focus, since doing so would undermine the point of the film, they still feel like caricatures that don't seem realistic. They never show you small glimpses on how he's able to actually to transform this class. Still... As melodramatic as the entire subplot where he takes in a young runaway, you still have to admire just how heartfelt it is. In fact, I would argue and say they could've made a better film if it had focused solely on this. ( Which again, works to a fault because it shows just how much they try to cram things in... ) This cast was surprisingly stacked. James Caan reminded me how much I missed him. I shouldn't have lost it when I saw Isaiah Whitlock Jr. thinking he was going to say his immortal line. You can't deny that it's just a surface level dramatized view of just how terrible the education system within this country is. Nihilistic, but there is truth to it. I'd argue and say it's even worse than that. No matter what, there is absolutely no way in hell that I would work for any group beyond middle school. I always thought it took a special kinda person to want to teach those grades. Another one of those depressing films that don't offer you any true solutions by the end of it. Still makes me happy I was raised in the suburbs. "The worst part about this job is that nobody says thank you"...yeah, I can't even make a stupid joke about that...I felt that one...

o substituto é um filme que me interessa muito mais pela ferida que existe por trás de sua própria forma do que pela maneira como ele tenta falar sobre educação. porque tony kaye faz um filme sobre um professor substituto que entra numa escola pública em crise, mas filma esse ambiente como se estivesse entrando num lugar onde todas as pessoas já chegaram emocionalmente depois do fim do mundo. não existe propriamente a promessa de transformação pedagógica. existe exaustão. adrian brody é perfeito pra isso porque o personagem praticamente já chega interpretado pela própria postura corporal. henry não entra naquela escola com a energia do professor idealista que vai descobrir sua vocação. ele entra como alguém que aprendeu a não criar raízes. o título, é menos uma característica profissional do que uma estratégia de sobrevivência. ele observa alunos, colegas, familiares e desconhecidos, mas tenta não se deixar possuir por nenhum deles. a ironia é que o próprio ato de observar acaba produzindo vínculos que ele gostaria de evitar. e kaye filma essa distância de maneira muito particular. o filme parece estar constantemente oscilando entre documentário, drama televisivo, videoclipe, ensaio visual e diário subjetivo. tem câmera na mão, animação, desenhos sobre a imagem, fotografias, textos, imagens em baixa definição, cortes abruptos, planos que parecem ter sido arrancados de um arquivo pessoal. às vezes isso é poderoso porque dá a sensação de que estamos dentro de uma consciência fragmentada. outras vezes é excessivo, porque kaye parece tão ansioso pra comunicar o estado emocional do personagem que a própria forma começa a gritar aquilo que a atuação já estava dizendo. esse é, pra mim, o grande problema e também a grande virtude do filme. tony kaye é um diretor que não parece confiar na neutralidade da câmera. ele quer que cada sequência carregue uma posição emocional. em a outra história americana , isso aparecia através da manipulação formal e do contraste entre preto e branco e cor. aqui ele leva essa tendência pra um território ainda mais subjetivo. a escola não é simplesmente uma instituição filmada. ela é quase uma paisagem mental da alienação contemporânea. o problema é que o roteiro às vezes reduz essa complexidade a uma série de afirmações bastante explícitas. o filme quer falar sobre professores desvalorizados, adolescentes abandonados, famílias ausentes, burocracia educacional, sexualização precoce, depressão, pobreza e a transformação da escola em uma instituição que precisa administrar problemas sociais muito maiores do que ela consegue resolver. tudo isso é legítimo. mas frequentemente o filme parece ter medo de que o espectador não tenha entendido, então coloca outra camada de sofrimento por cima. isso fica especialmente evidente na maneira como alguns estudantes são construídos. há momentos em que eles parecem menos personagens do que manifestações de determinados problemas sociais. a garota prostituída, a adolescente que procura afeto, o aluno agressivo, a professora esgotada. o filme possui uma indignação genuína, mas às vezes sua indignação transforma pessoas em símbolos. é uma diferença importante: quando o filme observa uma pessoa sofrendo, ele pode ser devastador; quando precisa explicar o significado daquele sofrimento, torna-se muito mais convencional. e tem algo bastante curioso na relação entre henry e os alunos justamente porque ele tenta não ser o “salvador”. isso diferencia de boa parte do subgênero do professor inspirador. não existe uma grande sequência em que o professor encontra a técnica pedagógica perfeita e muda uma turma inteira. henry sabe que uma pessoa sozinha não consegue consertar uma estrutura social quebrada. ele pode escutar alguém, oferecer algum cuidado, impedir uma pequena tragédia, mas não pode transformar a escola em outra coisa. isso dá ao filme uma dimensão política interessante, mesmo quando ele se torna sentimental demais. a escola aparece como o lugar onde todas as falhas da sociedade chegam ao mesmo tempo. professores precisam lidar com alunos cuja vida doméstica está destruída, adolescentes procuram nos outros aquilo que não recebem em casa, administradores respondem a estatísticas e avaliações, famílias transferem responsabilidades. a escola não criou necessariamente essas condições. ela simplesmente é o lugar onde elas se tornam impossíveis de ignorar. por isso eu gosto particularmente das cenas em que o filme deixa de discursar e simplesmente acompanha henry trabalhando. existe uma tensão entre cuidar dos outros e não conseguir cuidar de si mesmo que brody sustenta muito bem. a voz baixa, o olhar cansado, a maneira como ele ocupa os espaços. ele não interpreta um homem vazio. interpreta alguém que construiu o vazio deliberadamente pra não precisar encarar aquilo que existe por baixo. e aí mercedes, a jovem prostituída torna essa contradição ainda mais dolorosa. a relação entre os dois funciona porque henry não consegue simplesmente permanecer um observador. ele reconhece nela uma vulnerabilidade que desperta algo que sua filosofia de distanciamento não consegue controlar. ao mesmo tempo, o filme precisa tomar cuidado pra não transformar essa relação em uma fantasia de redenção masculina, e felizmente tem momentos em que ele consegue preservar a assimetria e o desconforto da situação. o avô de henry também é essencial pra compreender o personagem. o passado não aparece apenas como informação biográfica, mas como aquilo que torna impossível pra ele permanecer completamente desprendido. o filme vai revelando que o “ substituto ” não nasceu de uma filosofia sofisticada. nasceu de trauma, culpa e perda. e isso é muito mais interessante do que a superfície de “professor desencantado”. por outro lado, existe uma espécie de romantização da depressão e do sofrimento que considero problemática. às vezes parece acreditar que quanto mais devastada estiver uma pessoa, mais profundamente humana ela é. a fotografia, a trilha, a montagem e as performances trabalham constantemente pra elevar a dor ao estatuto de experiência quase poética. em seus melhores momentos isso produz uma melancolia genuína. nos piores, parece que o filme está transformando sofrimento em estética. essa ambivalência é muito tony kaye. ele é um cineasta profundamente emocional, mas sua emoção frequentemente vem acompanhada de uma necessidade quase compulsiva de tornar visível a emoção. ele não quer apenas que você perceba que alguém está triste. quer que a textura da imagem fique triste, que a montagem fique triste, que o desenho fique triste, que a música fique triste. às vezes é lindo. às vezes é como alguém sublinhando três vezes uma frase que já estava sublinhada. no fim, acho que o título acaba sendo mais importante do que toda a retórica sobre educação. henry passa o filme tentando se manter separado do mundo, como se observar fosse uma maneira de não sofrer. mas a própria experiência de ensinar demonstra o contrário: olhar verdadeiramente pra outra pessoa já é uma forma de envolvimento. você pode se recusar a salvar o mundo, e provavelmente deve, porque ninguém consegue, mas não consegue observar uma pessoa em sofrimento indefinidamente sem que alguma coisa dentro de você responda. e talvez o filme seja mais forte justamente nessa contradição. henry quer ser espectador de uma sociedade em colapso, mas descobre que não existe posição neutra diante da dor. tony kaye pode exagerar, sentimentalizar e transformar sua indignação em espetáculo, mas é difícil dizer que ele não acredita profundamente naquilo que está filmando.
Bom filme, bem construído, boas cenas, abre muito à interpretação pessoal, bons atores. Senti um apelo à estética gótica, porém, nada que atrapalhe de verdade o enredo do filme.

“A child’s intelligent heart can fathom the depth of many dark places. But can it fathom the delicate moment of its own detachment?” An “of its time” movie if I’ve ever seen one, early 2010s to its core. A predictable script sometimes lacking nuance, yet pristinely workable with stunning monologues littered throughout. The editing was surprisingly experimental, too; its use of mixed media and varied speed and colour added that extra bit of depth, and the wide angles were so jarring. I went in expecting a moving tale of the distressing complexities of being a teacher (think ‘Half Nelson’, ‘Steve’) but boy did Tony Kaye take this up a few notches. ‘Detachment’ covers so many bases you really don’t know which way it will turn next. Ultimately it is a simple encapsulation of how trauma is felt so profoundly, so vastly. It is generational and deeply cyclical, the ripple effect hard to avoid. Devastating on all accounts, but cynically hopeful (oh how I love a paradox). I, too, feel like a non-person.

"I'm not here,you may see me but I'm hollow" حين يصبح الابتعاد وسيلة للبقاء هناك أفلام تحاول أن تشرح لنا العالم، وهناك أفلام تجعلنا نشعر بثقله دون أن تمنحنا فرصة للهروب منه. وفيلم Detachment ينتمي إلى النوع الثاني؛ فهو ليس مجرد فيلم عن التعليم أو عن معاناة المعلمين والطلاب، بل تأمل مؤلم في الإنسان حين يصبح محاصرًا بين ما يشعر به وما يستطيع التعبير عنه، وبين حاجته إلى الآخرين وخوفه من الاقتراب منهم. منذ عنوانه، يضع الفيلم أمامنا فكرة أساسية: الانفصال العاطفي. ذلك الابتعاد الذي قد يبدو في البداية نوعًا من القوة أو السيطرة على الذات، لكنه قد يكون في الحقيقة وسيلة دفاع يلجأ إليها الإنسان بعدما يصبح الألم أكبر من قدرته على احتماله. فأحيانًا لا يبتعد الإنسان لأنه لا يحتاج إلى أحد، بل لأنه يحتاج إلى الآخرين أكثر مما يستطيع الاعتراف به. وأحيانًا لا يكون الصمت دليلًا على البرود، بل محاولة أخيرة لحماية ما تبقى من روح أنهكتها التجارب. ### الفكرة — عالم مليء بالناس، لكنه عاجز عن التواصل يتناول الفيلم عالم التعليم من زاوية تتجاوز المناهج والدرجات والنجاح الأكاديمي. فالمدرسة هنا ليست مجرد مكان لنقل المعرفة، بل مساحة تتقاطع فيها معاناة الطلاب، وعجز المعلمين، وضغوط المجتمع، وتلك المسافة المتزايدة بين الإنسان والإنسان. هنري بارثس، الذي يؤدي دوره أدريان برودي، معلم بديل ينتقل بين المدارس دون أن يسمح لنفسه بالانتماء الكامل إلى أي مكان. يبدو هادئًا ومتماسكًا، لكنه يحمل داخله ماضيًا مؤلمًا يجعله مترددًا في بناء علاقات عميقة مع الآخرين. إنه يعرف كيف يستمع، وكيف يفهم ألم الناس، لكنه يجد صعوبة في السماح لأحد بأن يقترب من ألمه الخاص. وهنا تكمن المفارقة التي يمنحها الفيلم عمقًا إنسانيًا كبيرًا: قد يكون الإنسان قادرًا على فهم الآخرين، لكنه عاجز عن إنقاذ نفسه. وقد يمنح الآخرين الكلمات التي يحتاجون إليها للاستمرار، بينما لا يجد الكلمات المناسبة ليواجه بها حياته. الفيلم لا يصور هنري باعتباره بطلًا مثاليًا أو شخصًا يمتلك إجابات عن كل شيء؛ بل يقدمه إنسانًا يحاول أن يؤدي دوره في عالم لا يعرف كيف يتعامل مع جراحه. وهذا ما يجعل شخصيته مؤثرة؛ لأنها لا تنتمي إلى عالم الأبطال الخارقين، بل إلى عالم الأشخاص الذين يواصلون حياتهم رغم أنهم لا يعرفون تمامًا كيف يفعلون ذلك. ### الإبداع في الطرح — الألم الذي لا يحتاج إلى صراخ من أكثر الجوانب إبداعًا في Detachment طريقته في تصوير المعاناة النفسية. فهو لا يعتمد دائمًا على الأحداث الكبيرة أو المواجهات المباشرة، بل يمنح التفاصيل الصغيرة مساحة واسعة كي تكشف ما تعجز الشخصيات عن قوله. تتداخل الصور والذكريات والحوارات والمونولوجات لتخلق إحساسًا بأننا لا نشاهد العالم من الخارج فقط، بل نقترب من الطريقة التي يراه بها إنسان مثقل بتجاربه. والمدرسة، بما تحمله من فوضى وضغوط وعلاقات متوترة، تصبح صورة مصغرة لمجتمع يعاني من أزمة أعمق: أزمة في القدرة على الإصغاء، وفي فهم احتياجات الآخرين، وفي الاعتراف بأن وراء كل سلوك إنسانًا له قصة لا نعرفها. إن الإبداع هنا ليس في تقديم فكرة جديدة تمامًا، بل في الطريقة التي تتشابك بها الأفكار الإنسانية مع الأسلوب السينمائي. فالفيلم يستخدم صورًا وتكوينات بصرية غير تقليدية ليجعلنا نشعر بالاضطراب الداخلي للشخصيات، وكأن الشكل نفسه أصبح امتدادًا لحالتها النفسية. ### التمثيل — أداء يحمل ما لا تقوله الكلمات يقدم أدريان برودي أداءً هادئًا ومشحونًا بالمشاعر المكبوتة. فهو لا يعتمد على الانفعالات الصاخبة بقدر ما يعتمد على النظرات، والتردد، ونبرة الصوت، والمسافة التي يتركها بين شخصيته وبين العالم المحيط بها. إن هنري شخصية يصعب فهمها بالكامل، وهذا جزء من قوتها. فكلما حاولنا الاقتراب منها، اكتشفنا أن هناك شيئًا لا تستطيع قوله، أو ربما لا تعرف كيف تقوله. وتقدم بيتي كاي، في دور إيريكا، حضورًا إنسانيًا مؤلمًا يضيف إلى الفيلم بعدًا آخر من أبعاد الإهمال والوحدة والحاجة إلى الحنان. ومن خلال الشخصيات المحيطة بهما، لا تبدو المعاناة حكرًا على فرد واحد، بل حالة تتخذ أشكالًا مختلفة، وتترك آثارًا متفاوتة في كل إنسان. قوة التمثيل في الفيلم تكمن في أنه لا يجعل الشخصيات مجرد أدوات لإيصال رسالة اجتماعية؛ بل يمنحها تناقضاتها وضعفها واحتياجاتها، حتى نشعر أن لكل منها حياة كاملة تتجاوز حدود الشاشة. ### الأثر النفسي — حين نكتشف أن الصمت ليس دائمًا سلامًا ربما أكثر ما يجعل الفيلم مؤثرًا هو أنه يضعنا أمام أشكال مختلفة من الوحدة. هناك من يختار الابتعاد عن الآخرين، وهناك من يُترك وحيدًا رغم محاولاته المستمرة للتواصل، وهناك من يعيش وسط الناس لكنه يشعر بأنه غير مرئي. والفيلم يجعلنا نتساءل: كم مرة مررنا بجانب إنسان ولم ننتبه إلى ما يحمله داخله؟ وكم مرة فسرنا صمت شخص بأنه عدم اهتمام، بينما كان في الحقيقة عاجزًا عن التعبير؟ وكم مرة أخفينا نحن أنفسنا خلف الهدوء، لأننا لم نعرف كيف نطلب المساعدة؟ إنه لا يطلب منا أن نبرر كل تصرف مؤلم، ولا أن نعتبر كل شخص ضحية بلا مسؤولية؛ بل يدعونا إلى أن نكون أكثر انتباهًا إلى التعقيد الإنساني الذي لا يظهر دائمًا على السطح. ومع ذلك، لا يقدم الفيلم الانفصال العاطفي باعتباره حلًا ناجحًا. فهو يكشف ثمنه أيضًا: أن تحمي نفسك من الألم قد يعني أحيانًا أن تحرمها من القرب والدفء والانتماء. وأن تتجنب التعلق بالآخرين قد يجنبك بعض الخسارات، لكنه قد يجعلك تخسر أشياء لا يمكن تعويضها. ### الخاتمة — أن تبقى إنسانًا رغم كل شيء Detachment ليس فيلمًا يمنحك شعورًا مريحًا بأن كل شيء سينتهي على ما يرام. إنه فيلم يتركك أمام أسئلة ثقيلة عن التعليم، والمجتمع، والطفولة، والوحدة، وعن قدرة الإنسان على الاستمرار حين لا يجد من يفهمه. لكنه، وسط كل هذا الألم، لا يخلو من لحظات إنسانية تذكّرنا بأن التواصل، مهما بدا صعبًا، يظل ممكنًا. وأن مجرد رؤية شخص آخر، والإصغاء إليه، والاعتراف بمعاناته، قد يكون أمرًا أكثر أهمية مما نتخيل. إن Detachment هو حكاية الإنسان الذي يبتعد عن العالم كي لا ينكسر، ثم يكتشف أن الابتعاد نفسه قد يكون شكلًا آخر من أشكال الانكسار. إنه فيلم عن أولئك الذين يواصلون أداء أدوارهم في الحياة، بينما يحملون في داخلهم أشياء لم يستطيعوا مواجهتها بعد. وعن أولئك الذين يمنحون الآخرين ما كانوا يتمنون أن يحصلوا عليه هم أنفسهم. وربما أكثر ما يبقى منه بعد المشاهدة هو هذا السؤال: هل نبتعد عن الآخرين لأننا لم نعد نحتاج إليهم، أم لأننا نخشى أن نحتاج إليهم ثم نفقدهم؟ قد لا يقدم الفيلم إجابة نهائية، لكنه يجعلنا ندرك أن الإنسان، مهما حاول أن يبدو مكتفيًا بنفسه، يظل بحاجة إلى أن يُرى، وأن Além de ser um homem solitário cheio de traumas e problemas para resolver, ele não deixa de se preocupar com o próximo. Pra mim fica evidente quando ele traz Erica pra casa, uma adolescente que vendia seu corpo nas ruas por dinheiro, ele tenta ajuda-lá porque sabe que ela não tá ali por prazer ou porque acha certo, ela tá ali por abandono, falta de instrução. E por ter visto a mãe dele se matar de overdose, ele talvez se enxergasse um pouco nela (erica) na perspectiva de ser uma pessoa lidando com problemas e enxerga também a própria mãe nela porque sabe que para ela se matar assim como fez a mãe dele é muito provável. Erica’s attachment to Henry, Meredith’s trauma and depression, Henry’s own emotional detachment—there was something in all of it that felt disturbingly familiar. But one small, almost overlooked scene hit me harder than anything else. Mr. Watt, a teacher whose presence seems invisible to everyone around him—even his own family. When Henry asks, “Are you alright?” he simply asks, “You see me?” Henry replies, “Yeah, I see you.” His response—“Oh God, it’s so relentless. Thank you.”—is devastating. Such a tiny moment, yet it says so much about loneliness and the desperate need to simply be noticed. That scene genuinely stayed with me.

Incrível como Carl Lund conseguiu nos inserir em sua narrativa melancólica e reflexiva desde o começo da obra. Se você já esteve em uma escola pública, realmente conversou com seus professores e já os imaginou fora da sala de aula, você se conecta de forma muito maior com a obra, pois aquele ambiente, infelizmente, é muito familiar. A atuação e a direção desse filme foram impecáveis. Não há uma cena em que eu não estivesse sentindo tristeza ou refletindo sobre ela. É como se Carl soubesse exatamente o que estava fazendo; utilizou seus recursos magistralmente. Acredito que o maior tópico discutido seja a falta de esperança e ambição. A classe baixa é empurrada a ser realista desde criança, pois até para se sonhar é preciso ter dinheiro. Isso acaba fazendo com que as pessoas se tornem alheias e prefiram estar sempre anestesiando suas dores, não importa a forma, apenas para evitar pensar sobre o futuro apático que as aguarda. Outro tema, não menos importante na obra, foi como todos temos nossas dores. Quando Henry fala para Meredith que, no futuro, as coisas melhoram, fica claro que nem ele nem ela acreditavam nisso. Nessa cena, fica clara a mensagem principal do filme: todos temos nossas dores e devemos tentar encontrar paz com elas, pois são algo que estará sempre conosco. Diferentemente de outros filmes, este não termina com um final feliz e tudo se resolvendo, já que seu objetivo é mostrar a realidade nua e crua. O filme não esconde isso nem por um minuto, o que o torna lindo e único.

I expected this to be primarily about the school system and while it of course is, on a broader scale it feels like it tackles generational divide more than anything. The youth are expected to learn and be guided by those who came before, but what of the problems plaguing that generation? How can you teach and guide when you feel aimless and lost yourself? Being older does not inherently mean being wiser, and so often these people are thrust into a position of responsibility when they were never given the guidance they’re now expected to pass on. These issues chain all the way back through the generations that came before and they will continue to all those that will follow. At one point do you change from the person who is guided to the one who guides, and what do you do if you’re wholly unprepared for that? Until we can solve that question, the kids really don’t stand a chance.

Этот фильм мне делает очень больно, как будущему педагогу. Но и открывает глаза, показывает правду этой профессии. У меня много мыслей и чувств, а это показатель отличного кино. Главная мысль заложена в его названии. Detachment (отсраненность) – это щит. Это попытка Генри сказать себе: «Я здесь временно. Я не буду вовлекаться. Это не мои дети, это не моя жизнь». Но фильм наглядно демонстрирует, что абсолютная отстраненность это иллюзия. Это история о кризисе человечности и тотальном одиночестве. О том, как тяжело быть значимым взрослым для тех, кого предали собственные родители. О том, что дети впитывают наше безразличие и превращаются в монстров или добровольно уходят из жизни. «Некоторые из нас верят, что могут сделать мир лучше. Но иногда мы приходим в себя, и понимаем, что не смогли.» «Мы обязаны вести наших детей, чтобы они не гибли. Не оказывались на обочине. Не становились ненужными.» «Мы не смогли. Мы подвели всех. Включая себя.» И самое главное, это кино о сверхчеловеческом учительском труде. В конце фильма разрушенный, заваленный мусором и сухими листьями класс – это визуальное воплощение краха школы. Демонстрация того, во что превратилось государственное образование: заброшенное, опустошенное место, где спасение детей встало на второй план. Учителя перестали пытаться, смирившись с тем, что (показанная в фильме) школа предоставлена для «отбросов», как выразилась сама директор. Кроме всего вышесказанного, мы можем увидеть наглядно, что у каждого учителя есть своя жизнь и проблемы помимо школы. Я уверена, что мало кто задумывается об этом (легче сказать что учительница «сучка, которой муж не даёт»). Мисс Мэдисон пытается искренне сопереживать, но ученики буквально плюют ей в лицо. Она плачет в туалете от бессилия, потому что её запаса любви не хватает на то, чтобы перекрыть их домашний ад. Доктор Паркер – школьный психолог, которая срывается на крик от того, что дети абсолютно глухи к своему будущему, а их родителям наплевать. Мистер Чарльз стал невидимкой для учеников. Чтобы его хоть как-то заметили, он вынужден совершать безумные поступки (например, пить лекарство, стоя на столе). Фильм показывает, что учитель — это самый незащищенный человек в системе. Общество требует от них быть святыми и спасителями, но не дает им никакой психологической защиты взамен. Педагогика это не для всех. Каким бы ты ни был прекрасным учителем, ты должен быть готов к неблагодарности и жестокости этой системы, не теряя своей собственной жизни в стенах и ловя хорошие моменты в хаосе.

This film had me messed up. There's a scathing humanity to it, it asks you to pay extreme attention to the people around you and what they're going through. It asks you to take a lens to our education system. It asks you to take a lens to the faculty, to the inner demons we take to work, bring back home and never speak about. It renders what happens to children when they're left behind and it's not light handed, it's heart crushing. There's some Camus stuff going on, there's 1984 , and there's even discussion about The Fall of the House of Usher . It's a difficult watch. The hard part about art is someone will probably say it goes too far, it's not deep enough, it's just too cynical, or something to that tune. But it was affecting and at times even inspiring how much the film wants you to think about other people and what you might be/might not be doing to help them. And, how hard it can be to help others when you're still in the throes of helplessness yourself. I think Mr. Henry is trying to stay detached because of his past and because it doesn't always work in your favor to attach yourself to anything or anyone. But it shows that it can be ultimately beneficial or inadvertently disastrous and you can't possibly know until you try. One of my favorite parts: You alright? What? You see me? You see me standing here? Yeah I see you. Oh god, it's so relentless. Thank you.
